note: User Expire blocks accounts either per-user on a set date (stored in the user_expire DB table) or per-role after N seconds of inactivity (config user_expire.settings:user_expire_roles). Warning emails are governed by send_expiration_warnings, offset (secs before expiry), and frequency (secs between sends). Blocking runs on hook_cron. Live-state cases are config-based (role rules + warning settings) because saving user entities on this shared site currently fatals in an unrelated module (salesforce_example); the per-user table workflow is documented and covered by recipe cases. Configure route user_expire.admin; permissions set user expiration / view expiring users report / administer user expire settings.

evals.prompt: Using the user_expire module, how do I make a single Drupal user account automatically get blocked on a specific date, and what permission is needed to set that?
evals.expected_output: With the 'set user expiration' permission, edit that user's account; a 'User expiration' section lets you tick a box and choose an expiration date. The date is stored (as a Unix timestamp) in the user_expire database table keyed by uid, and hook_cron blocks the account once the date passes.

evals.prompt: In the user_expire module, which configuration controls blocking accounts after a period of inactivity per role, and what does a value of 0 mean?
evals.expected_output: The user_expire.settings:user_expire_roles map holds, per role machine name, the number of seconds of inactivity before accounts with that role are blocked. A value of 0 (or an absent role) means that role never expires. Inactivity is measured from last access (or account creation if never logged in).

evals.prompt: Where can an administrator see which user accounts are about to expire on a site running the user_expire module, and what permission gates that page?
evals.expected_output: The Expiring users report at /admin/reports/expiring-users (route expiring_users.admin), gated by the 'view expiring users report' permission, lists accounts that have a pending expiration date.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, user_expire has been configured to expire one role's accounts after a period of inactivity. Inspect the live configuration and state which role machine name has an inactivity expiration set.
evals.expected_output: The content_editor role has an inactivity expiration of 7776000 seconds (90 days) in user_expire.settings:user_expire_roles. Check with `drush config:get user_expire.settings user_expire_roles`.

evals.prompt: Is this site's user_expire module currently sending account-expiration warning emails to users? Inspect the live configuration and state the value of the relevant setting.
evals.expected_output: No: user_expire.settings:send_expiration_warnings is false on the live site, so no expiration warning emails are sent (drush config:get user_expire.settings send_expiration_warnings).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure the user_expire module so that authenticated users are automatically blocked after 90 days of inactivity. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set user_expire.settings:user_expire_roles['authenticated'] to 7776000 (90 days in seconds) — via the per-role field on /admin/config/people/user-expire or by editing the config. Verified when the authenticated key equals 7776000.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure user_expire's expiration-warning emails to begin 14 days before an account expires and to be re-sent no more often than once per day. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set user_expire.settings:offset = 1209600 (14 days) and frequency = 86400 (1 day), both in seconds. Verified when offset is 1209600 and frequency is 86400.
